summary: Phase 149O.20L.7D.10 -- Repaired-Source Redeployment + Action-9 Amendment Independent Authorization Verification. Independent verification only (no Dell mutation, no venv/wrapper change, no CHGR mutation, no DeploymentBinding, no certification, no activation). Independently re-derived, not trusted from 7D.9's own summary: candidate SHA 28bf137b5dc95d024e8913b678dce0501a46fd0f authenticity and ancestry (despite its own misleading commit subject, git merge-base --is-ancestor proves it contains 7D.7's actual repair commit 73ea8b23); exact repaired bytes for the three verifier modules, byte-identical to current HEAD; zero authority-relevant drift; contract versions HBDC-001 v1.0/HMIC-001 v1.3/HMRC-001 v1.1 unchanged (HMIC-001 byte-identical across old-deployed/candidate/HEAD); the candidate's own tracked-tree inventory (4108 paths, 4097x100644, 11x100755), enumerated fresh from a disposable git worktree, not inherited from the old 4030/4024/6 figures; HMIC frozen-source membership of all three repaired modules, read from the live production module; the implementation_scope_digest change (b728d368... -> 4e3452ba...), independently recomputed by calling derive_implementation_scope_digest() directly against three disposable worktree roots -- exact match to 7D.8's/7D.9's own reported values. Fresh, read-only SSH to hac-dell (machine-id 54ff22ce400b475aa0d55cb68f4a3334) reconfirmed zero drift from the 7D.8/7D.9 baseline: source pinned at 7a3fa971... (detached, clean, 4030-path mode mapping intact), wrapper digest b3e969...c32 unchanged, venv .pth/direct_url.json still path-bound not byte-bound, zero DeploymentBinding; an apparent /bin and /sbin mode-777 anomaly was investigated and resolved as a non-issue (both are symlinks to root:root 755 targets, independently confirmed pcae-unwritable) -- no shadow-executable PATH surface exists. Independently confirmed the candidate object is not yet present in Dell's local git store (a real network fetch will be required at forward-execution time) while the old object is confirmed locally present (rollback prerequisite satisfied). Reproduced the exact proposed forward-then-rollback sequence in a disposable local clone with the remote deliberately severed before the rollback step -- rollback succeeded with zero network access, narrowing 7D.9's claim to exactly the authorized bounded sequence rather than an unlimited 'Git never garbage-collects it' assertion; git count-objects -v confirmed zero packable/garbage objects, and an explicit rollback-anchor ref was independently judged unnecessary given the old SHA's own reflog-backed reachability. Independently read chgr-0e37ed1340b14311826722c4dbf3e856 and its confirmation/provenance/integrity artifacts directly from disk (not merely cited): governance-record verify --related passes all seven applicable checks (schema_shape, digest_self_consistency, lifecycle_structural_legality, confirmation_binding, assurance_truthfulness, provenance_consistency, integrity_consistency); the record's own decision_subject and rationale text bind the full 40-character candidate SHA and the exact corrected Action-9 PATH, not an external unbound reference, and explicitly disclose the NOT-CERTIFIED-FOR-BOUNDARY-C consequence. Independently reconstructed all three decision-session attempts from their own persisted JSON: confirmed CDS-a2e437a8's subject_ref is genuinely 574 characters (exceeds the CHGR-001 schema's 500-character limit) and CDS-9fac483e used a genuinely unregistered template_ref; confirmed no readiness/publication artifact anywhere references either abandoned session id (no contamination) and that exactly one other, unrelated, one-day-earlier CHGR (chgr-d4343fa5..., a 149O.20L.7B.2 Boundary-P record) exists alongside the two historical CHGRs already known, ruling out a mistaken fifth-record contamination reading. Independently confirmed neither chgr-96a0ce12... nor chgr-541cb08c... authorizes this transition, from each record's own decision_subject/rationale text and publish-time ordering (chgr-541cb08c...'s publish timestamp independently reconfirmed to precede the repair commit), and reasoned through an explicit old/new collision attack finding no valid fallback path. Traced the architecture-status 'no explicit Recommended next phase sentence' limitation to PROJECT_STATUS.md's own prose-completeness gap for the 7D.9 entry specifically (the canonical phase report and phase-completion-metadata.json both already agree on 7D.10 as next phase) -- classified as derived-status incompleteness only, not touched, per verification-only scope. Two non-blocking findings disclosed: the CHGR confirmation record's election and confirmation captured_at timestamps are identical to the microsecond (a typed_confirmation_only, L0-assurance capture mechanism, not a defect, though the decision-session's own eight-stage pipeline including separate ConfirmationRequest/ConfirmationValidation stages is independently confirmed structurally distinct); and the 7D.9 proposition document itself was never amended to record the actual election (its own text remains frozen with a 'HUMAN ELECTION REQUIRED -- NOT YET DECIDED' placeholder) even though the separately-verified CHGR record does carry full, independently-checked authority -- a documentation-currency gap, not an authority gap. Independent companion test module (does not import 7D.9's own test module as oracle): 25 passed, 0 failed. Final verdict: VERIFIED AUTHORIZED FOR REPAIRED-SOURCE REDEPLOYMENT + ACTION-9 RE-ADJUDICATION. Recommends 149O.20L.7D.11 (real redeployment + Action-9 re-adjudication execution) next; 149O.20L.7E remains blocked until 7D.11 succeeds and measures exactly {HBDC-REQ-042}.
